--- title: "Day 9: DPD and GMM" author: "Robert W. Walker" date: "07/30/2026" categories: [panel data, code, analysis] image: "image.jpg" --- ## Slides - [A reveal presentation](https://robertwwalker.github.io/Essex26-2J-Slides/ESSSSDA26-Day9/) ## The I() construct `?formula` gives you insights into the way to structure generic formula objects in R. The `I()` construct is a consistent and clear way in R's foundations to specify functional operations on variables. ## R and GMM There are a number of packages for estimating GMM models in R. `pgmm` does many of the most basic models, though Stata is the industry leader in this. That said, there is a relatively new and highly customizable package for this: `pdynmc` which is [described here in a pdf vignette](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/pdynmc/vignettes/pdynmc-intro.pdf). What follows is a detailed example with a software guide. # Software Guide and Example A (hopefully) practical reference for estimating dynamic panel data (DPD) and generalized method of moments (GMM) models. It covers the full range of estimators discussed in the course, from basic difference GMM through slope-heterogeneity tests and nonlinear dynamic models. Where one environment handles something the other cannot, that is noted explicitly. This page is a practical reference for estimating dynamic panel data (DPD) and generalized method of moments (GMM) models. It covers the full range of estimators discussed in the course, from basic difference GMM through slope-heterogeneity tests and nonlinear dynamic models. Where one environment handles something the other cannot, that is noted explicitly. ## Package and command ecosystem ### R packages Install once; load at the top of each script. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} install.packages(c( "plm", # core panel estimators: pgmm, pmg, pcdtest "panelvar", # panel VAR with impulse responses "lme4", # mixed models for nonlinear DPD (CRE logit, Poisson) "fixest", # fast FE Poisson and high-dimensional FE "marginaleffects", # average partial effects from nonlinear models "dplyr", # data manipulation (also in tidyverse) "kableExtra" # formatted output tables )) ``` ::: ::: {.callout-important} ## The `lag()` conflict between `plm` and `dplyr` `dplyr` exports `lag()` with a scalar-only `n` argument. `plm` exports `lag()` that accepts vector ranges like `1:2`, which `pgmm()` formulas require. Loading both packages without intervention causes: ``` Error in lag(): ! n must be a whole number, not an integer vector. ``` **Fix**: add `lag <- plm::lag` once after loading both packages. This is done in the hidden setup chunk for this document. **Separate issue**: `plm::lag` applied to a plain numeric vector inside `dplyr::mutate()` returns the input **unchanged** — it does not compute a positional lag. Always use `dplyr::lag()` explicitly in pipeline code: ```r df |> group_by(id) |> mutate(y_lag = dplyr::lag(y, 1)) # correct df |> group_by(id) |> mutate(y_lag = lag(y, 1)) # wrong when lag <- plm::lag ``` ::: ### Stata commands Built-in commands ship with Stata. Community-contributed commands must be installed once via `ssc install`. ```stata * ---------- built-in commands ---------- * xtabond Arellano-Bond difference GMM (one- or two-step) * xtdpdsys System GMM (Arellano-Bover / Blundell-Bond) * xtdpd General DPD — most flexible built-in specification * xtregar AR(1) FE/RE (not GMM; included for comparison) * xtivreg Panel IV (not full GMM) * xtprobit Random-effects probit * xtpoisson Random-effects Poisson / fixed-effects Poisson * xtset id year -- always declare panel structure first * ---------- community commands (install once) ---------- ssc install xtabond2 // Roodman (2009): collapse, orthog. devs., diff-in-Hansen ssc install xtlsdvc // Bruno (2005): bias-corrected LSDV ssc install xtpmg // Pesaran-Shin-Smith (1999): MG and PMG estimators ssc install xtdcce2 // Ditzen (2021): dynamic CCE ssc install xtcd2 // Ditzen (2021): Pesaran CD test ssc install xtslope // Eberhardt (2012): Pesaran-Yamagata slope homogeneity ssc install panelhet // alternative slope homogeneity tests ssc install pvar // Abrigo-Love (2016): panel VAR ssc install ivreg2 // extended IV/GMM (often needed alongside xtabond2) ``` --- ## Data preparation Both environments use the Layard-Nickell UK manufacturing employment data (`abdata` in Stata; `EmplUK` in the `plm` package). ::: {.panel-tabset} ### R ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(plm) library(dplyr) data(EmplUK) # Log-transform and declare panel structure EmplUK <- EmplUK |> mutate(n = log(emp), w = log(wage), k = log(capital), ys = log(output)) pdat <- pdata.frame(EmplUK, index = c("firm", "year")) # Set lag <- plm::lag for pgmm formula parsing (done in setup; shown here # so the code is explicit when copying chunks to a standalone script) lag <- plm::lag # Precompute lag columns used by plm(model = "random") formulas. # These must live in pdat so they are available to static-r. # (Using lag() inside a RE formula with lag <- plm::lag causes # swar_Between_check() to fail; precomputed columns avoid this.) pdat$n_lag1 <- plm::lag(pdat$n, 1) pdat$n_lag2 <- plm::lag(pdat$n, 2) pdat$w_lag1 <- plm::lag(pdat$w, 1) pdim(pdat) # panel dimensions: N, T, balanced? ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Unbalanced Panel: n = 140, T = 7-9, N = 1031 ``` ::: ::: ### Stata ```stata use abdata, clear // ships with Stata; n w k ys already logged xtset id year // declare panel structure; always do this first xtdescribe // shows panel balance / gaps xtsum n w k ys // within / between / overall variance decomposition ``` ::: --- ## Within and between variation ::: {.panel-tabset} ### R ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # panel_summary() defined in the setup chunk; apply to each log variable result <- sapply(c("n","w","k","ys"), function(v) panel_summary(EmplUK[[v]], EmplUK$firm)) t(result) |> kbl(caption = "Variance decomposition: 140 UK firms, 1976-1984") |> kable_styling(font_size = 13) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}

````` ::: ::: ### Stata ```stata xtsum n w k ys ``` ::: --- ## Static panel baseline (for comparison) Always estimate pooled OLS and fixed effects before GMM. They bracket the true $\gamma$: OLS is upward-biased (omitted $\alpha_i$); FE is downward-biased (Nickell). GMM estimates should lie between them. ::: {.panel-tabset} ### R ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Use precomputed lag columns (n_lag1, n_lag2, w_lag1 from setup). # Avoids swar_Between_check() failure that occurs when lag <- plm::lag is # active and lag() appears inside a random-effects formula. # Pooled OLS (upward-biased gamma) ols <- plm(n ~ n_lag1 + n_lag2 + w + w_lag1 + k + ys, data = pdat, model = "pooling") # Two-way fixed effects (downward Nickell bias) fe <- plm(n ~ n_lag1 + n_lag2 + w + w_lag1 + k + ys, data = pdat, model = "within", effect = "twoways") # Random effects — individual effects only. # Two-way RE with a lagged DV is numerically fragile (Swamy-Arora # between-estimator fails when between-transform of lag(n) ≈ between-transform # of n itself). Individual RE is the sensible baseline comparison. re <- plm(n ~ n_lag1 + n_lag2 + w + w_lag1 + k + ys, data = pdat, model = "random", effect = "individual") # Hausman test: FE vs RE phtest(fe, re) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Hausman Test data: n ~ n_lag1 + n_lag2 + w + w_lag1 + k + ys chisq = 16.846, df = 6, p-value = 0.009868 alternative hypothesis: one model is inconsistent ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} summary(fe) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Twoways effects Within Model Call: plm(formula = n ~ n_lag1 + n_lag2 + w + w_lag1 + k + ys, data = pdat, effect = "twoways", model = "within") Unbalanced Panel: n = 140, T = 5-7, N = 751 Residuals: Min. 1st Qu. R-Squared: 0.55779 F-statistic: 182.837 on 6 and 599 DF, p-value: < 2.22e-16 ``` ::: ::: ### Stata ```stata * Pooled OLS reg n L(1/2).n w L.w k ys i.year * Two-way fixed effects xtreg n L(1/2).n w L.w k ys i.year, fe * Random effects (individual only — see note on two-way RE above) xtreg n L(1/2).n w L.w k ys, re * Hausman test estimates store re_est xtreg n L(1/2).n w L.w k ys i.year, fe hausman . re_est ``` ::: --- ## Anderson-Hsiao: IV estimator Anderson and Hsiao (1981) first-difference to remove fixed effects, then instrument $\Delta y_{i,t-1}$ with $y_{i,t-2}$ (level) or $\Delta y_{i,t-2}$ (difference). Useful pedagogically as the conceptual predecessor to AB. ::: {.panel-tabset} ### R ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # First-difference by hand. # MUST use dplyr::lag() explicitly here — plm::lag() on a plain vector # inside mutate() returns the input unchanged, not a positional lag. pdat_fd <- EmplUK |> group_by(firm) |> arrange(year) |> mutate( Dn = n - dplyr::lag(n, 1), # Delta y_t DLn = dplyr::lag(n,1) - dplyr::lag(n,2), # Delta y_{t-1} (endogenous) Dw = w - dplyr::lag(w, 1), ln2 = dplyr::lag(n, 2), # y_{t-2}: level instrument DLn2 = dplyr::lag(n,2) - dplyr::lag(n,3) # Delta y_{t-2}: diff instrument ) |> ungroup() |> filter(!is.na(DLn2)) pdat_fd_p <- pdata.frame(pdat_fd, index = c("firm","year")) # AH estimator using plm() IV formula syntax: y ~ endog | instruments # Level instrument y_{t-2} ah_level <- plm(Dn ~ DLn + Dw | ln2 + Dw, data = pdat_fd_p, model = "pooling") summary(ah_level) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Pooling Model Instrumental variable estimation (Balestra-Varadharajan-Krishnakumar's transformation) Call: plm(formula = Dn ~ DLn + Dw | ln2 + Dw, data = pdat_fd_p, model = "pooling") Unbalanced Panel: n = 140, T = 4-6, N = 611 Residuals: Min. 1st Qu. Median 3rd Qu. Max. -9.718 -0.746 -0.233 0.685 10.244 Coefficients: Estimate Std. Error z-value Pr(>|z|) (Intercept) 0.59693 7.36842 0.0810 0.9354 DLn 12.12574 136.76771 0.0887 0.9294 Dw -1.65679 12.76065 -0.1298 0.8967 Total Sum of Squares: 12.6 Residual Sum of Squares: 1653.2 R-Squared: 0.057866 Adj. R-Squared: 0.054767 Chisq: 0.505502 on 2 DF, p-value: 0.77666 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} # Difference instrument Delta y_{t-2} ah_diff <- plm(Dn ~ DLn + Dw | DLn2 + Dw, data = pdat_fd_p, model = "pooling") summary(ah_diff) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Pooling Model Instrumental variable estimation (Balestra-Varadharajan-Krishnakumar's transformation) Call: plm(formula = Dn ~ DLn + Dw | DLn2 + Dw, data = pdat_fd_p, model = "pooling") Unbalanced Panel: n = 140, T = 4-6, N = 611 Residuals: Min. 1st Qu. R-Squared: 0.15336 Chisq: 81.358 on 2 DF, p-value: < 2.22e-16 ``` ::: ::: ### Stata ```stata * First-difference; instrument with lagged level y_{t-2} ivregress 2sls D.n (D.L.n = L2.n) D.w, vce(robust) * Instrument with lagged difference Delta y_{t-2} ivregress 2sls D.n (D.L.n = LD.n) D.w, vce(robust) * ivreg2 gives first-stage F, Cragg-Donald, Kleibergen-Paap weak instrument tests ivreg2 D.n (D.L.n = L2.n) D.w, robust first ``` ::: --- ## Arellano-Bond: difference GMM Arellano and Bond (1991) use all valid lagged levels as GMM instruments. The global `lag <- plm::lag` (set in the setup chunk) makes `pgmm()` formulas work correctly throughout. ### Formula syntax for `pgmm()` Left of `|`: model covariates with lag structure. Right of `|`: GMM-type instruments via `lag(var, min:max)`, where `2:99` means all available lags from 2 onward. ### One-step Arellano-Bond ::: {.panel-tabset} ### R ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Replicates Arellano-Bond (1991) Table 4(a1) # lag() resolves to plm::lag (set globally in setup) -- pgmm formulas work ab_one <- pgmm( log(emp) ~ lag(log(emp), 1:2) + lag(log(wage), 0:1) + lag(log(capital), 0:2) + lag(log(output), 0:2) | lag(log(emp), 2:99), data = EmplUK, effect = "twoways", model = "onestep" ) summary(ab_one) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Twoways effects One-step model Difference GMM Call: pgmm(formula = log(emp) ~ lag(log(emp), 1:2) + lag(log(wage), 0:1) + lag(log(capital), 0:2) + lag(log(output), 0:2) | lag(log(emp), 2:99), data = EmplUK, effect = "twoways", model = "onestep") Unbalanced Panel: n = 140, T = 7-9, N = 1031 Number of Observations Used: 611 Residuals: Min. 1st Qu. LSDVC (Bruno 2005) has no maintained CRAN implementation. # Best approach in R: triangulate FE (lower bound) and AB (consistent). fe_est <- plm(n ~ n_lag1 + n_lag2 + w + w_lag1 + k + ys, data = pdat, model = "within", effect = "twoways") ab_est <- pgmm( log(emp) ~ lag(log(emp),1:2) + lag(log(wage),0:1) + log(capital) | lag(log(emp),2:4), data = EmplUK, effect = "twoways", model = "twosteps" ) cat("FE gamma1:", round(coef(fe_est)["n_lag1"], 4), " [downward-biased]\n") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` FE gamma1: 0.6734 [downward-biased] ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} cat("AB gamma1:", round(coef(ab_est)[1], 4), " [consistent]\n") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` AB gamma1: 0.0415 [consistent] ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} cat("LSDVC lies between these; use xtlsdvc in Stata for the bias-corrected point estimate\n") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` LSDVC lies between these; use xtlsdvc in Stata for the bias-corrected point estimate ``` ::: ::: **R limitation**: Bruno (2005) LSDVC is Stata-only. Use `panelvar::pvargmm()` with `transformation = "fod"`. ### Stata ```stata xtabond2 n L.n L(0/1).w L(0/1).k yr1980-yr1984, /// gmm(L.n, lag(2 99) collapse) /// iv(L(0/1).w L(0/1).k yr1980-yr1984) /// twostep robust small /// orthogonal ``` ::: --- ## Panel VAR ::: {.panel-tabset} ### R ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(panelvar) # data(EmplUK) EmplUK$n <- log(EmplUK$emp) EmplUK$w <- log(EmplUK$wage) # Panel VAR: employment and wages jointly endogenous # Use transformation = "fod" to handle EmplUK's unbalanced structure pvar_mod <- pvargmm( dependent_vars = c("n", "w"), lags = 1, transformation = "fod", data = EmplUK, panel_identifier = c("firm", "year"), steps = "twosteps", system_instruments = FALSE, max_instr_dependent_vars = 4, min_instr_dependent_vars = 2 ) summary(pvar_mod) # Stability: characteristic roots inside unit circle stability(pvar_mod) # Generalised impulse response functions pvar_irf <- girf(pvar_mod, n.ahead = 8, ma_approx_steps = 8) plot(pvar_irf) ``` ::: ### Stata ```stata * ssc install pvar pvar n w, lags(1) fod twostep pvarstable pvarirf, oirf mc(500) step(8) pvargranger ``` ::: **Software note**: R's `panelvar` provides richer IRF, stability diagnostics, and forecast-error variance decomposition than Stata's `pvar`. The formal Pesaran-Yamagata (2008) Delta-tilde test is not on CRAN. # Approximation: run unit-by-unit OLS, inspect coefficient dispersion. unit_coefs <- lapply(split(EmplUK, EmplUK$firm), function(d) { d <- d |> arrange(year) |> mutate(n_l1 = dplyr::lag(n,1), n_l2 = dplyr::lag(n,2), w_l1 = dplyr::lag(w,1)) |> filter(!is.na(n_l2)) if (nrow(d) < 5) return(NULL) tryCatch(coef(lm(n ~ n_l1 + n_l2 + w + w_l1 + k + ys, data=d)), error = function(e) NULL) }) unit_coefs <- do.call(rbind, Filter(Negate(is.null), unit_coefs)) cat("Coefficient of variation across units (informal heterogeneity check):\n") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Coefficient of variation across units (informal heterogeneity check): ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} round(apply(unit_coefs, 2, function(x) sd(x, na.rm=TRUE) / abs(mean(x, na.rm=TRUE))), 3) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` (Intercept) n_l1 n_l2 w w_l1 k 15.025 14.605 6.899 11.274 43.201 329.284 ys 2.811 ``` ::: ::: **R limitation**: Use `xtslope` in Stata for the formal Pesaran-Yamagata $\tilde\Delta$ test statistic with correct inference. ### Stata ```stata * ssc install xtslope xtslope n L.n w L.w k ys // Delta and Delta-tilde statistics + p-values ``` ::: ### Mean Group and Common Correlated Effects MG ::: {.panel-tabset} ### R ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Use `xtdcce2` in Stata. ### Stata ```stata * ssc install xtdcce2 xtdcce2 n L.n w k ys, cr(n w k ys) cr_lags(1) // pooled CCE xtdcce2 n L.n w k ys, cr(n w k ys) cr_lags(1) mg // CCE-MG (heterogeneous) ``` ::: --- ## Nonlinear dynamic panel models: binary and count outcomes ### Data construction ::: {.panel-tabset} ### R ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Create a binary DV and compute Mundlak / Wooldridge (2005) terms. # MUST use dplyr::lag() explicitly — plm::lag() on a plain vector # inside mutate() does not compute a positional lag. panel_df <- EmplUK |> mutate(n_hi = as.integer(n > median(n, na.rm = TRUE))) |> group_by(firm) |> arrange(year) |> mutate( n_hi_lag = dplyr::lag(n_hi, 1), # lagged binary DV y_init = first(n_hi), # initial condition y_{i1} w_bar = mean(w, na.rm = TRUE), # unit mean of wage (Mundlak term) k_bar = mean(k, na.rm = TRUE) ) |> ungroup() |> filter(!is.na(n_hi_lag)) cat("Observations after setup:", nrow(panel_df), "\n") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Observations after setup: 891 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} cat("Binary DV mean:", round(mean(panel_df$n_hi), 3), "\n") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Binary DV mean: 0.492 ``` ::: ::: ### Stata ```stata xtile n_hi = n, nq(2) replace n_hi = (n_hi == 2) bysort id (year): gen y_init = n_hi[1] bysort id: egen w_bar = mean(w) bysort id: egen k_bar = mean(k) ``` ::: ### Dynamic logit: Wooldridge (2005) CRE approach Wooldridge (2005) conditions on the initial value $y_{i1}$ to proxy the distribution of $\alpha_i$, yielding a standard RE logit (or probit) augmented with $y_{i1}$ and unit-means $\bar{x}_i$ as additional covariates. Logit is used here rather than probit for numerical stability; the approach and interpretation are identical. ::: {.panel-tabset} ### R ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(lme4) # Wooldridge (2005) CRE dynamic logit # y_init proxies distribution of alpha_i; w_bar, k_bar are Mundlak terms mod_logit <- glmer( n_hi ~ n_hi_lag + w + k + y_init + w_bar + k_bar + (1 | firm), data = panel_df, family = binomial(link = "logit"), control = glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", optCtrl = list(maxfun = 2e5)) ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` boundary (singular) fit: see help('isSingular') ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} summary(mod_logit) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Generalized linear mixed model fit by maximum likelihood (Laplace Approximation) [glmerMod] Family: binomial ( logit ) Formula: n_hi ~ n_hi_lag + w + k + y_init + w_bar + k_bar + (1 | firm) Data: panel_df Control: glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", optCtrl = list(maxfun = 2e+05)) AIC BIC logLik -2*log(L) df.resid 176.0 214.3 -80.0 160.0 883 Scaled residuals: Min 1Q Median 3Q Max -5.1566 -0.0509 -0.0036 0.0911 18.5576 Random effects: Groups Name Variance Std.Dev. firm (Intercept) 0 0 Number of obs: 891, groups: firm, 140 Fixed effects: Estimate Std. probit and logit give equivalent inferences) xtprobit n_hi L.n_hi w k y_init w_bar k_bar, re * APEs margins, dydx(L.n_hi w k) predict(pu0) * Test initial condition test y_init * RE logit xtlogit n_hi L.n_hi w k y_init w_bar k_bar, re margins, dydx(L.n_hi w k) predict(pr) ``` ::: ### Dynamic Poisson / count models ::: {.panel-tabset} ### R ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # CRE Poisson: Wooldridge (2005) / Blundell-Griffith-Windmeijer (2002) approach # Use emp (count) as outcome; include y_init as initial-condition control pois_df <- EmplUK |> group_by(firm) |> arrange(year) |> mutate( emp_lag = dplyr::lag(emp, 1), y_init = first(emp), w_bar = mean(w, na.rm = TRUE), k_bar = mean(k, na.rm = TRUE) ) |> ungroup() |> filter(!is.na(emp_lag)) mod_pois <- glmer( emp ~ emp_lag + w + k + y_init + w_bar + k_bar + (1 | firm), data = pois_df, family = poisson, control = glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa") ) summary(mod_pois) # FE Poisson via fixest (consistent, no incidental-parameters bias for Poisson) # library(fixest) # fe_pois <- fepois(emp ~ emp_lag + w + k | firm + year, data = pois_df) ``` ::: ### Stata ```stata * CRE Poisson xtpoisson emp L.emp w k y_init w_bar k_bar, re margins, dydx(*) predict(nu0) * FE Poisson (Hausman-Hall-Griliches 1984 — no incidental-parameters problem) xtpoisson emp L.emp w k, fe ``` ::: --- ## Capability matrix | Estimator / Feature | R (`plm`) | R (other) | Stata built-in | Stata (`ssc`) | |---|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:| | Anderson-Hsiao IV | `plm` IV formula | — | `ivregress` | `ivreg2` | | AB one-step diff. It supersedes `xtabond`, `xtdpdsys`, and `xtdpd` and is the only command with collapsed instruments, orthogonal deviations, and difference-in-Hansen. **`plm::pgmm()` is the R workhorse** but has three hard gaps: no collapsed instruments, no orthogonal deviations, no difference-in-Hansen. For panels where these matter, call `xtabond2` via Stata. **LSDVC and PMG belong to Stata**. Bruno (2005) bias-corrected LSDV (`xtlsdvc`) and Pesaran-Shin-Smith (1999) Pooled Mean Group (`xtpmg`) have no maintained CRAN implementations. **Slope heterogeneity diagnostics are Stata-favoured**. The formal Pesaran-Yamagata $\tilde\Delta$ test (`xtslope`) and Dynamic CCE (`xtdcce2`) have no direct CRAN equivalents. `plm::pmg(model = "cmg")` provides CCE-MG estimation but without the full DCCE workflow. **Nonlinear DPD is well-handled in both** environments via the Wooldridge (2005) CRE approach. `lme4::glmer()` in R and `xtlogit/xtprobit/xtpoisson, re` in Stata implement the same estimator. Use `marginaleffects::avg_slopes()` in R and `margins` in Stata for average partial effects — always report APEs, not latent-index coefficients.
